nina (eng-arch): Heads up — I sketched a lightweight follow-up to the packaging RFC: micro-bundles for tiny patch delivery + operator-friendly rollback hooks. want feedback before I turn it into a formal RFC.
caleb (platform): SGTM. quick question: are micro-bundles orthogonal to seed/delta workflow or a replacement for small deltas?
nina (eng-arch): orthogonal. idea: keep the manifest/delta graph but allow a signed 'micro-bundle' that contains a tiny set of diffs + an activation manifest. ships faster over constrained airgap pipes.
ryan (infra): so it's basically bundling only changed model shards + minimal activation plan. how do you handle partial apply failures? that's the hard part for offline ops.
marta (onprem): this is the part ops care about. we need deterministic rollback that doesn't require fetching older blobs from the internet. prefer dual-image swap semantics where possible.
caleb (platform): tradeoff: dual-image gives easy rollback but doubles disk/registry footprint. micro-bundles aim to avoid that by shipping inverse-patch info so operator can undo locally.
sam (sre): inverse-patch sounds brittle for complex binary blobs. can we instead lean on staged-activation + tombstone markers so operator can fail into previous runtime without full disk copy?
nina (eng-arch): yes — two approaches sketched:
1) inverse-patch included in bundle (small, deterministic apply/undo)
2) activation fence + tombstone + operator-level revert that toggles activation pointer
both need signed manifests and a safe window.
ryan (infra): example activation flow would help. can you paste a toy operator hook?
nina (eng-arch): pasted a minimal sketch:
```
kind: MicroBundle
metadata:
  name: mb-2026-03-09
spec:
  patches:
    - path: models/v2/shard-12.bin
      hash: sha256:abcd...
      apply: patch-12.delta
      inverse: patch-12.inverse
  activation:
    fence: true
    activate_after: 30m
    rollback_marker: tombstone://mb-2026-03-09
  signature: sig-v1:...
```
marta (onprem): looks useful. ops ask for a 'dry-run' CLI hook that validates the bundle apply without flipping activation pointer. please add to RFC.
caleb (platform): also include metrics we can emit: microbundle.apply.count, apply.duration, revert.count, revert.duration, failed-apply-reason — those go in console and onprem operator telemetry.
sam (sre): preflight checks: disk space estimate, shard-hash-validate, operator-lock-acquire. if any fail, abort and emit clear remediation steps.
ryan (infra): about signing: prefer layered sigs — bundle signed by infra signer, activation manifest signed by customer key. that way infra can't silently activate customer clusters.
opsec-bot: Note: cross-signer activation requires KMS policy change. file an access-control ticket before enabling in private deployments.
caleb (platform): UX question: should micro-bundles be a new artifact type in the manifest repo or a special-case delta with metadata? pros/cons?
nina (eng-arch): pros for new artifact type: explicit intent, separate lifecycle, simpler operator code. cons: additional index entries and new registry semantics for airgap tooling.
marta (onprem): ops prefer explicit type. less surprise when debugging.
sam (sre): one more: can we add a safety leash — if apply fails during activation window N times, auto-roll back and mark bundle quarantined. add to operator playbook.
ryan (infra): agreed. add 'quarantine' state with operator annotation and opt-in auto-roll-back threshold.
caleb (platform): final ask: include a migration path in RFC for existing delta consumers. i.e., how to produce micro-bundles from current delta pipeline with minimal maint overhead.
nina (eng-arch): noted. I'll draft a follow-up RFC section: conversion tool + synth inverse patches + test harness (fuzz apply/undo). planning to include a simple e2e demo for onprem QA.
marta (onprem): can you also add a short runbook for hotfix-without-net? ops often need a recipe for top-of-stack fixes when offline.
nina (eng-arch): will do. thanks all — i'll iterate and drop a link to the draft RFC here shortly. :+1:
caleb (platform): thanks — ping when ready and we'll schedule a short design review.
sam (sre): +1, want to validate failure modes with chaos tests.
opsec-bot: Reminder: any change touching activation signatures needs compliance review for air-gapped customers. Submit a compliance checklist.
